tasks.question: Within godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_world.gd, every terrain feature this file scatters (crests, boulders, spires, trees, landmarks, anchors) is only placed after passing through one specific function that decides whether a candidate site is valid, checking clearance from both the racing line and the camera path in a single call. Identify: (a) the exact symbol responsible for that combined placement-validity decision, (b) its kind, (c) its exact line span on this checkout, (d) the exact lower-level symbol(s) it calls to measure each of the two clearances, and (e) the smallest surrounding implementation body a change to how placement validity is decided would need to touch. Do not include the sibling function that only explains a rejection in human-readable form without itself deciding validity.
tasks.why_tests_provider_utility: environment_world.gd is 1618 lines with ~28 static functions. A structural symbol index (Ctags or tree-sitter) can answer 'what functions exist and where' in one bounded query, versus Grep needing several pattern guesses (_sited, _clear, _track_gap, _why all match loosely-related search terms) and Read needing to page through a large file. This is the profile Benchmark C2's own design predicted a provider should plausibly help with, and which C2 never actually tested because the provider was never called.

tasks.target_symbol: action_clearance() defined independently in 4 files under godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/ and .../v2/
tasks.question: Four separate marble-machine part files -- godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/hero_bowl.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/hero_collector.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/hero_finish.gd, and godot/assets/marble_machine/v2/v2_bowl.gd -- each define their own static func action_clearance() -> Dictionary, describing the cylindrical volume around that part that must stay clear of structure. Identify: (a) the exact symbol, file, kind, and line span of each of the four definitions; (b) for each one, the exact shape/centre/radius/height formula it returns; (c) which of the four are identical to each other in their returned formula structure (same constant names and same numeric offsets) and which are distinct, grouping them accordingly. Do not include any file that only calls action_clearance() on another module's object without defining its own version of the function.
tasks.why_tests_provider_utility: action_clearance is defined independently, verbatim-same-name, in exactly 4 files -- a single find_definition('action_clearance') call on EITHER provider returns all 4 definition sites (file+line for Ctags; file+span+body for tree-sitter) in one bounded call (confirmed by deterministic dry run: Ctags 271 chars/4 matches, tree-sitter 1130 chars/4 matches with full bodies). Solving part (c) rewards body-level comparison, which tree-sitter provides directly and Ctags requires a small follow-up Read for. Neither provider's contribution depends on caller/reference resolution: the two aggregator files that only CALL action_clearance() (hero_machine.gd, v2_machine.gd) are excluded by checking whether each candidate file itself defines the symbol, not by tracing who calls whom.

tasks.reason: Required identifying every production CALLER of toy_geometry.gd's beam_section()/channel_section() across 36 candidate files, aliases, and a same-name local shadow. This is fundamentally a cross-file caller/reference-resolution problem. Confirmed via source-code audit (ctags_provider.py, treesitter_provider.py) and a deterministic dry run that neither Ctags nor tree-sitter has any caller/reference capability for GDScript -- both explicitly and honestly report it unavailable rather than emulating it. A forced provider call on this task would measure mandatory-call overhead, not provider value. Original question/hashes retained below for the record, not deleted.
tasks.original_question: Two mesh cross-section builder functions defined once in godot/scripts/toy_geometry.gd -- beam_section() and channel_section() -- are called from other production scene-building GDScript files (files that construct an actual Node3D/mesh scene, not diagnostic or reporting scripts) to build swept support and channel geometry. Identify every production scene file that calls either function, and for each one: every call site's enclosing symbol and line, and which of the two functions it calls (a file may call one, the other, or both, more than once). Do not include a file merely because it preloads/references toy_geometry.gd for unrelated geometry helpers. Do not include a file whose own locally-defined function happens to share one of these two names without actually calling toy_geometry.gd's version.
